newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Stg/mark faces firm barrier at 2.8040/60.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Stg/mark faces firm barrier at 2.8040/60.

text.p: Resilient sterling faces minor resistances on the way back up 2.80 marks, but attempts to extend the upside further might be thwarted by a tough barrier in the 2.8040/60 area, chartists said.
The pound's slump on Wednesday to a low of 2.7740 was seen as a chance to buy at lower levels, with chart signals still pointing to another attempt at the 4-1/2 year high at 2.8231, hit on April 15.
"The first leg of the uptrend completed at 2.81 and the subsequent correction is a chance to buy for next leg up to 2.8250," said Eddie Matts, director at Capital Management UK.
At 0711 GMT the pound was at 2.7920/30 marks and $1.6257/67, up from 2.7768/73 and $1.6220/30 in late Europe on Wednesday.

Howard Wright, chief analyst at Prisma Market Analysts, is bearish on the pound as long as it holds below a weekly pivot point at 2.8020. A break of 2.8020 would almost certainly foce a re-test of the 2.8160 level, he said.
If the pound fails at 2.8020, it is likely to ease to the April 7 breakaway gap at 2.7630, said Wright.
Cable completed a short-term topping pattern on Wednesday after eroding support at $1.6300/20. It stopped just below $1.62, keeping trendline support around $1.6180 area intact.
Cable's near-term health depends on holding the $1.6200/6180 support area, analysts said. If eroded, another prop is around the late March low at $1.6145.

On the upside, a break of $1.63 would be needed to reassert pressure on congestive resistance at 1.6350/60 ahead of the key barrier at $1.6400, a near three-week high which capped sterling on Tuesday.
Matts at Capital Management said the pound was likely to be confined at this stage by the $1.63 pivot point as the move accelerates below $1.6180.
